text:
Evgeni Malkin is 40, the Penguins are struggling, and the headlines are about where he fits if Pittsburgh sells. Daily Faceoff asked what happens to him as the team "inches toward fire sale," Minnesota and Vancouver outlets floated trade fits, and NDTV Sports reported he is expected to stay.

On the ice, he's still useful. He has 17 points in 18 games at 17.7 minutes a night, scoring at 3.2 points per 60, which is top-six production. His goals (6) match his chances (5.0 expected), and there are no luck flags on him either way. His last ten games went for 11 points, two of them goals.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows how he does it now: 10.6 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 96th percentile among forwards, and 55% of his shots off the rush. Evolving-Hockey liked his offense (his team created 0.22 more expected goals per 60 with him on) and disliked his defense (opponents got 0.19 more, bottom 4%). He's a playmaker with a cost, on a team deciding what it is. We'd watch the standings as much as the box score.
headline: Malkin keeps producing amid the sell-off talk
